reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes domain wall pinning at grain and twin boundaries in a different material system (medium-entropy alloys) and context (magnetic domain evolution, not a first-order magnetostructural transition). It does not provide direct support for the key premises about nucleation, transition breadth, or hysteresis reduction in FeMnNiGeSi films, nor does it address the effect of thermal processing on these features.
premises: Grain boundaries and twin/phase interfaces control nucleation and propagation of the magnetostructural transition in FeMnNiGeSi films.
Increased density of these microstructural features broadens the transition and reduces hysteresis.
Thermal processing (annealing/quenching) can modify grain boundary and interface density without altering composition or long-range chemical order.
Finer grains (from shorter/lower-temperature anneals) will yield a broadened transition with reduced hysteresis compared to as-deposited films.
